Topic: Real-world hybrid practice
Story (story.md): Microsoft ExP (2017): Bayesian and frequentist agreed on ~95% of A/B decisions. Booking.com mixes the two by context. FDA/EMA accept Bayesian for rare-disease and adaptive trials, still require frequentist primary for most phase 3.
Technical (chapter.md): Not covered (story-only real-world framing).

Topic: Framework choice is operational, not theological
Story (story.md): Each org picks a lens based on data shape, cost of error, and audit trail, not ideology.
Technical (chapter.md): Chapter framing: which rule a team writes down depends on what kind of call it is.

Topic: The two decision rules in the wild
Story (story.md): Frequentist: ship if p < 0.05 and point estimate > 0. Bayesian: ship if P(lift > MMU) > 0.95.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Try: same two rules, with MMU = 0.5pp drawn from Ch 8's minimum meaningful uplift.

Topic: Apples-to-apples caveat: MMU gate asymmetry
Story (story.md): Story note: the two rules as teams write them aren't structurally matched; a matched frequentist rule (point estimate > MMU) shrinks the borderline gap, showing most disagreement is the gate, not the lens.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A note: wild rules aren't structurally matched (F has no meaningfulness gate, B does). Simulator also records a matched F rule, ship if p < 0.05 AND point estimate > MMU, to separate lens effect from MMU effect.

Topic: Population of true effects drives the numbers
Story (story.md): Story note: bell-shaped population of true effects centered at zero drives the numbers; heavy-tailed, skewed, or mostly-zero populations would shift the sharpness of the verdicts.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Population caveat: true_diff drawn from Normal(0, 1pp). ~38% of mass within ±MMU and ~95% within ±2pp. Heavy-tailed or skewed populations would shift the trade-offs.

Topic: Joint rule: ship only if both agree
Story (story.md): Story note: a joint rule (ship only when both lenses agree) tracks the more conservative lens, costing a few marginal wins in exchange for a defensible audit trail.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop E Try + Observe: joint ship rate tracks B's (the more conservative). At MMU and below, joint ships are rare; at truth in (0.010, 0.020] ~0.20; at (0.020, 0.050] ~0.60 (Wilson 95% CI ~0.45–0.74). Image joint_decision.png.

Topic: Framework wars are smaller than the question
Story (story.md): The question is the thing. A wrong question answered well with either lens is still wrong, a right question survives imperfect frameworks.
Technical (chapter.md): Distilled two-lens commentary: lenses are complementary, not competitors. Agreement on clear cases, divergence flags the borderline experiments worth a judgement call.
